scope: Manual fast/deep Scrape rejection at synchronous shared document replacement, before React's page-reset effect.
use_case: A dental practice captures its new-patient intake page while the same URL reloads to a new document.
cause: useScrape success checks both capture sequence and the synchronous shared page identity. Its exception handler checked only capture sequence, which changes later in React's effect. A deferred A rejection between identity replacement and that effect writes A's error into the current Scrape store.
hypothesis_results: Effect-order gap confirmed: changing shared page identity without rerendering, then rejecting the pending real hook call, produces A's capture error; unchanged-document failure correctly remains visible.
Wrong target ruled out for this reproduction: the first capture call targets document-a; no second capture or URL change is needed.
Successful stale result admission ruled out in the same seam: the existing same-URL success regression passes and the production success path already checks current page identity.
change: Capture the initiating identity outside the try so every exception checks its pageKey against the synchronous shared identity before publishing the error. The same catch handles fast capture, deep scrolling and deep capture exceptions.
regression_seam: Real useScrape hook, real Zustand Scrape store and real capture-error classification. Chrome capture is an external deferred boundary; the mocked identity snapshot changes before React's reset effect. Both fast/deep modes assert that stale errors are absent while unchanged-document errors preserve the captured message.
